blogs.title: Triple-Deck TAVI: When a Third Transcatheter Valve Is the Least Bad Option
blogs.description: This post would examine the decision to perform TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV in a patient with prohibitive surgical risk, prior valve degeneration, and treated prosthetic valve endocarditis. It would focus on the heart-team calculus: when redo surgery is theoretically standard but practically hazardous, how clinicians weigh anatomy, comorbidity, prior interventions, and patient goals to justify an off-label third transcatheter procedure.

blogs.title: CT Before the Third Valve: Planning for Coronary Obstruction, Neo-Skirt, and Future Access
blogs.description: This post would focus on preprocedural imaging strategy in serial transcatheter valve reintervention. It would cover how CT can be used to assess coronary ostial height, sinus dimensions, valve-to-coronary distance, frame interaction, anticipated neo-skirt, and implantation depth, and how these measurements informed the choice to proceed without coronary protection while still prioritizing future coronary reaccess.

blogs.title: After Endocarditis, Can You Go Back In? TAVI Reintervention Once Prosthetic Valve Infection Is Treated
blogs.description: This post would explore the tension between guideline preferences for surgery in prosthetic valve endocarditis and real-world management after infection resolution. It would discuss what constitutes adequate evidence that endocarditis is no longer active, how prior infection changes but does not necessarily preclude transcatheter reintervention, and why the management question shifts from microbiology to anatomy and hemodynamics once cure is established.

blogs.title: Beating Prosthesis-Patient Mismatch in a Valve-in-Valve-in-Valve Procedure
blogs.description: This post would examine the hemodynamic problem of layering three transcatheter valves inside one another, with particular attention to severe prosthesis-patient mismatch risk. It would discuss why a supra-annular self-expanding valve was selected, the rationale for high implantation at the level of the prior leaflet plane, the role of post-dilation, and how immediate high gradients may evolve over time after frame expansion and improved leaflet mechanics.

blogs.title: Commissural Alignment Is No Longer Optional: Lifetime Planning Starts with the First TAVI
blogs.description: This post would use the case to highlight the broader concept of lifetime structural valve management. It would discuss how commissural alignment, frame choice, coronary access, and reintervention trajectories become increasingly important as younger and longer-surviving patients accumulate prior valves, and why today's implant strategy must account for tomorrow's coronary angiography, valve failure, or redo intervention.

blogs.title: The Echo Trap After Complex Redo TAVI: Interpreting Early High Gradients Without Panicking
blogs.description: This post would focus on postoperative assessment and follow-up after complex transcatheter valve reintervention. It would analyze the striking finding of a very high immediate postprocedural gradient that improved substantially at 1 month and remained stable at 1 year, reviewing possible mechanisms, how to differentiate residual obstruction from evolving valve expansion, and how serial echocardiography can guide clinical confidence rather than premature reintervention.
